candidate_056.name: transition-local verification before durable memory mutation
candidate_056.mechanism_hypothesis: Treat every WRITE/REVISE/PRUNE of hard long-term memory as a state transition that must be locally checked for coverage of new evidence, preservation of still-valid prior content, and faithfulness to the current evidence or prior state before the mutation is admitted. Prefer ranking candidate transitions under the same prior state over relying only on final task reward or a scalar verifier score.

primary_evidence.source: TRUSTMEM: Learning Trustworthy Memory Consolidation for LLM Agents with Long-Term Memory, arXiv:2606.25161
primary_evidence.design: Mem-alpha validation ablations isolate action reward, efficiency reward, transition-verifier reward, and transition-ranked GRPO within the same framework; transition reliability is also evaluated on generated transition records.
primary_evidence.interpretation: This gives matched component-level evidence that supervising local memory transitions matters beyond merely optimizing final task reward. It directly strengthens candidate_055: source verification at admission is not enough if later revise/delete operations can silently omit, distort, or hallucinate persistent state.
primary_evidence.limits: Benchmarks are general long-term-memory tasks rather than autonomous science. Transition-error rates use a GPT-4o-mini judge, and the verifier is itself an LLM. The experiment does not establish that this exact verifier prevents scientific epistemic contamination or strategic lock-in.

candidate_056.status: New mechanism candidate with direct within-framework ablation evidence outside the science domain.
candidate_056.falsifier: A matched multi-seed scientific-agent memory study where transition-local coverage/preservation/faithfulness verification fails to improve held-out factual reliability or contamination persistence versus identical memory mutations without transition verification, after equalizing retrieval, model, context and compute.

candidate_057.name: provenance-linked two-tier authority with query-time sufficiency escalation
candidate_057.mechanism_hypothesis: Keep immutable raw/source-qualified evidence as the authoritative tier and treat compact summaries as lossy caches linked back to that authority. Answer cheaply from summary only when a sufficiency router judges the evidence adequate; otherwise escalate to raw evidence. Verified findings may be promoted back only with provenance links.

primary_evidence.source: From Lossy to Verified: A Provenance-Aware Tiered Memory for Agents, arXiv:2602.17913
primary_evidence.interpretation: The result supports separating cheap lossy memory from immutable evidence authority and allocating expensive evidence only when needed, rather than flattening all durable knowledge into summaries.
primary_evidence.limits: General conversational-memory benchmarks, not scientific agents. Main benchmark disables online write-back for all methods, so the causal benefit of verified promote-back itself is not established here. Accuracy remains below raw-only on LoCoMo.

candidate_057.relation_to_candidate_055_056: Candidate_055 controls what may first enter trusted memory; candidate_056 verifies each persistent mutation; candidate_057 separates lossy retrieval caches from immutable authority and escalates queries when the cache is insufficient. Their combined scientific-memory loop is a synthesis hypothesis, not a jointly tested system.
candidate_057.status: New architecture candidate with matched routing/efficiency evidence outside the science domain.
